questions.question: A bag has 10 marbles. All 10 are red. You pick one marble. What is the chance of getting a red marble?
questions.explain: If every marble in the bag is red, you will always get a red one. That makes it certain, not just likely.

questions.question: A bag has 10 marbles. All 10 are blue. You pick one marble. What is the chance of getting a green marble?
questions.explain: There are no green marbles in the bag, so you cannot get one. That makes it impossible.

questions.question: A bag has 10 marbles. 9 are red and 1 is blue. You pick one marble. What is the chance of getting a blue marble?
questions.explain: There is 1 blue marble out of 10, so it is hard to get but it can still happen. That is unlikely, not impossible.

questions.question: A bag has 10 marbles. 9 are red and 1 is blue. You pick one marble. What is the chance of getting a red marble?
questions.explain: 9 out of 10 marbles are red, so you are very likely to get red. But it is not certain because 1 marble is blue.

questions.question: Liam spins a spinner with 4 equal sections. Three sections are yellow and one is purple. What is the chance the spinner lands on yellow?
questions.explain: 3 out of 4 sections are yellow, so it is very likely to land on yellow. But it is not certain because 1 section is purple.

questions.question: Zoe spins a spinner with 2 sections. One tiny section is blue. One big section is red, three times bigger than the blue one. What is the chance it lands on blue?
questions.explain: The blue section is very small, so it is unlikely to land there. But it is still possible, so it is not impossible.

questions.question: A bag has 6 marbles. 5 are yellow and 1 is green. A friend says, 'You will definitely get yellow. It is certain.' What is wrong with that?
questions.explain: 5 out of 6 is a very good chance, but the 1 green marble means it is not guaranteed. So 'likely' is the right word, not 'certain.'

questions.question: A spinner has 4 equal sections. 3 are green and 1 is red. You spin it twice. What is the chance it lands on red both times?
questions.explain: Getting red once is already unlikely (1 out of 4). Getting it twice in a row is even less likely. But it can still happen, so it is not impossible.

questions.question: A spinner has 6 equal sections. 1 is purple and 5 are white. A friend says, 'Landing on purple is impossible because there are so many white sections.' Is your friend right?
questions.explain: There IS a purple section, so it can happen. But with only 1 out of 6, it is unlikely, not impossible.

questions.question: A bag has 7 marbles. 6 are red and 1 is blue. You pick one, note the colour, and put it back. What is the best word for the chance of getting red?
questions.explain: 6 out of 7 marbles are red, so it is very likely. But the 1 blue marble means it is not certain.

questions.question: Maya spins the prize wheel at her school fair. One big orange part covers almost the whole wheel. Two thin parts, blue and pink, fill the rest. What is the chance the arrow stops on orange?
questions.explain: Orange covers almost the whole wheel, so landing on orange is likely. It is not certain, because the arrow can still stop on a thin part.

questions.question: Noah's soccer bag holds 20 balls. 17 are blue and 3 are yellow. He grabs one ball without looking. What is the chance he grabs a yellow ball?
questions.explain: Only 3 balls out of 20 are yellow, so yellow is unlikely. It is not impossible, because there really are yellow balls in the bag.

questions.question: Ella keeps 8 foam cubes in a bag for math class. 3 of them are big and 5 are small. Every cube is red. What is the chance she pulls out a red cube?
questions.explain: All 8 cubes are red, so pulling out red is certain. The big and small counts do not change the colour, so red has to come out.

questions.question: Ravi spins the spinner in his board game. Four parts are yellow and very thin. One green part covers most of the spinner. What is the chance the arrow stops on yellow?
questions.explain: The four yellow parts are very thin, so together they cover only a little of the spinner and yellow is unlikely. Counting parts is not enough, because you must also look at how big each part is.
